criteria.criterion: athena-core has a Pinner trait with a real git-based implementation that resolves a repo URL and ref to a full 40-hex SHA and checks out that tree. The core, not an agent, makes the call.
criteria.evidence: Read the diff. crates/athena-core/src/pin.rs defines `trait Pinner` and `GitPinner`. GitPinner runs `git ls-remote`, then a depth-1 fetch, then `read-tree` and `checkout-index`, and checks the result with `is_full_sha`. The call is made in run.rs `Athena::pin_repo`, which is core code, not an agent.

criteria.criterion: The repo URL and ref come from the study instance's config (for example athena.toml). No firstmate URL or 'main' is hard-coded in Rust source; firstmate appears only as config or docs examples.
criteria.evidence: Read the diff. pin_repo reads `repo_url` and `repo_ref` from `jc.config.capability(id)`. These are new `CapabilityConfig` fields in athena-data/src/config.rs. Grep for `firstmate` in *.rs found no matches. firstmate appears only in a commented example in athena.toml. The only 'main' strings in the diff are in test fixtures (`git init -b main`).

criteria.criterion: run.rs calls the pinner only for the study capability, before the prediction commit. It stores URL, ref and SHA in a new optional Job record field. The change capability never calls the pinner.
criteria.evidence: Read the diff. pin_repo returns early unless `capability.pins_repo()` is true. The trait default is false; only Study overrides it to true. The call sits before the prediction commit's job record is built. `Job.pin: Option<PinnedRepo>` (url, ref, sha) uses serde default and is skipped when None.

criteria.criterion: The pinned tree is mounted read-only in the working directory of both producer and verifier. Docs say how read-only is enforced.
criteria.evidence: Read the diff. run.rs calls `mount(pin_dir, snapshot.dir())` for the producer and `mount(pin_dir, vsnap.dir())` for the verifier. `mount` copies the tree, adds it to info/exclude and removes the write bits. The pin.rs module docs and D75 both say enforcement is file permissions plus agent policy, not an OS mount.

criteria.criterion: A dispatch-level test builds Athena with a counting fake pinner and a scripted fake agent driver on the study capability. It asserts exactly one pinner call, the fake SHA in the Job record, and the mount existing in the agent working directory. Run `cargo test -p athena-core`.
criteria.evidence: Ran it. `run_pin_tests::a_study_pins_once_records_the_commit_and_mounts_it_read_only_for_both_agents` passed (33 passed, 0 failed). It asserts count()==1, the pin in the job record at both the dispatch commit and HEAD, and (Producer, exists, readonly) and (Verifier, exists, readonly) seen from the agents' working directories. It uses a stand-in capability with id "study" and `pins_repo` true, not the real Study type (see findings).

criteria.criterion: A dispatch-level test with the real Change capability and the same counting fake pinner asserts zero calls and no pin in the Job record. Run `cargo test`.
criteria.evidence: Ran it. `the_change_capability_never_pins` in athena-cli/tests/lifecycle.rs passed in both the filtered run and the full `cargo test` run. It uses the Fixture, which carries the real change capability, and asserts count()==0 and job.pin == None.

criteria.criterion: Real-pinner unit tests use a local file:// repo in a temp dir, with no network. They cover resolving the ref to the expected SHA, an error on a missing ref, and the read-only mount. Run `cargo test -p athena-core`.
criteria.evidence: Ran it. pin::tests `a_branch_a_tag_and_a_commit_resolve_to_their_commits`, `a_missing_ref_is_an_error` and `the_mount_is_read_only_and_invisible_to_git` all passed. Each uses a tempdir origin through a `file://` URL.

criteria.criterion: `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` pass. Removing the pin call in run.rs would fail at least one test.
criteria.evidence: Ran all three; all passed. Removing `self.pin_repo(...)` would leave pinner.count() at 0 and Job.pin as None, so the dispatch test's `assert_eq!(pinner.count(), 1)` would fail. This is from reading the test; I did not edit the code to try it.

criteria.criterion: The decision record (alternatives, reversal cost) is in docs/decisions.md and CHANGELOG.md notes the change. The diff has no secrets and no network-dependent tests.
criteria.evidence: Read the diff. D75 in docs/decisions.md has Decision, Alternatives (a–e), Tradeoff, Reversal cost and Provenance. CHANGELOG.md has an Added entry. The only URLs are example.com placeholders and file:// temp repos, and the test emails are noreply@example.com.

findings.summary: Nothing tests that the real Study capability opts into pinning.
findings.evidence: The dispatch test uses a stand-in `PinningStudy` with id "study". If `Study::pins_repo` in athena-cap-study were changed back to false, no test would fail, and the real study would silently skip pinning.

findings.summary: The study producer may run `chmod`, which can undo the read-only mount.
findings.evidence: In athena.toml the `[capabilities.study]` producer_commands include `chmod = ["*"]`. D75 discloses that the owner can chmod the mount. Because pinned-source/ is in info/exclude, such edits never reach the candidate, but the producer could still read altered source.

findings.summary: The test double module `fake` is public in the production library.
findings.evidence: lib.rs adds `pub mod fake;` without cfg(test) so the CLI integration tests can use CountingPinner. athena_agent::fake already follows the same pattern.

summary: The change passes. A study job now resolves its repository and ref, read from config, to a commit before it starts. The core does this through a Pinner trait, and the real implementation shells out to git. The pin is recorded in a new optional `pin` field of the Job record, and the pinned tree is mounted read-only at `pinned-source/` for both the producer and the verifier. The change capability never calls the pinner. Neither firstmate nor a branch is hard-coded in Rust source. I ran `cargo test -p athena-core`, the full `cargo test`, clippy with `-D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`, and all passed. The tests cover one pin call, the SHA in the record, the mount in both agents' working directories, zero calls for the change capability, and real-pinner tests on local `file://` repos (ref resolution, a missing ref, the read-only mount). Removing the pin call would fail the one-call assertion; I judged that by reading the test, not by editing the code. D75 and the CHANGELOG entry are present. Two minor findings: no test pins down that the real Study capability turns pinning on, and the study producer is allowed to run `chmod`, so it can make the mount writable again. That is disclosed, and it cannot affect the candidate.
